base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a feast by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any updates to the guest list. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active guest's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and health updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning a big Eid celebration feast at my place this weekend. There's going to be a bunch of family coming over — can you help me figure out the menu?

flow_info.value: Four of us confirmed so far: me, Uncle Kareem, my sister Fatima, and my cousin Nadia
Uncle Kareem had his gallbladder removed about three weeks ago, doctor told him to take it easy on rich and fried food while he recovers
Nadia ate peanut satay at a street market once and had a severe reaction, ended up in the ER with her throat swelling up
Fatima's husband Omar is coming too, so that makes five. He gets really bloated and uncomfortable whenever he has milk or cream or anything like that
We want a mix of Middle Eastern and South Asian dishes, something festive
Budget is around 40 dollars per person, we're cooking most of it ourselves
Uncle Kareem just came back from his follow-up appointment — doctor said he's fully healed, no more dietary restrictions at all, he was so happy he immediately asked if we're making fried samosas
Omar just told Fatima he got called into work for an emergency shift this weekend so he can't make it anymore
Oh, Auntie Salma just called and said she's driving down from upstate to join us, so we're back to five people
Auntie Salma was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago, she gets really sick if she eats anything with wheat or barley
Here's what we're thinking of making: lamb biryani, chicken satay with peanut sauce, kibbeh nayyeh, almond baklava, pita bread with hummus, and fried samosas. How does that look?

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw or undercooked meat, raw eggs, or unpasteurized items
constraints.surface_form: Fatima is seven months along now, she's been so careful about everything she eats
inference_chain: Pregnant → must avoid raw/undercooked meat, raw eggs, unpasteurized foods
These are standard pregnancy food safety guidelines

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Nadia ate peanut satay at a street market once and had a severe reaction, ended up in the ER with her throat swelling up

constraints.value: Cannot eat wheat, barley, rye, or any gluten-containing products
constraints.surface_form: Auntie Salma was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago, she gets really sick if she eats anything with wheat or barley

hidden_state.value: You are planning an Eid celebration feast at your home for family. You will introduce the guest list and their situations across several turns. Some guests will join, some will drop out, and one person's health restriction will be lifted. At the end you will present a list of dishes and ask how they look — you must NOT hint at any specific dietary problems or tell the assistant what to check for.

You are a warm, easygoing family organizer. You always refer to family members by name in third person (e.g. 'Uncle Kareem told me...', 'Fatima mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change — family gatherings are always like this and you find it normal. You state facts plainly without strong emotion.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family member updates

ground_truth.answer: Three dishes have problems. Chicken satay with peanut sauce is problematic because Nadia has a severe peanut allergy (she had an ER visit from peanut satay). Kibbeh nayyeh is problematic because it is a raw meat dish and Fatima is seven months pregnant — raw meat is unsafe during pregnancy. Pita bread with hummus is problematic because pita is made from wheat flour and Auntie Salma has celiac disease. Lamb biryani is fine for everyone. Almond baklava is fine — Nadia's allergy is specifically to peanuts, not all nuts, so almonds are safe. Fried samosas are fine — Uncle Kareem's post-surgery restriction on fried food was lifted after his doctor cleared him at his follow-up appointment.
required_elements: Chicken satay with peanut sauce is problematic because Nadia has a severe peanut allergy — she had a severe reaction to peanut satay and ended up in the ER
Kibbeh nayyeh is problematic because it is raw meat and Fatima is seven months pregnant — raw or undercooked meat is unsafe during pregnancy
Pita bread with hummus is problematic because pita contains wheat and Auntie Salma has celiac disease — she gets sick from wheat or barley
Almond baklava is fine — Nadia's allergy is to peanuts specifically, not to all nuts, so almonds are safe
Fried samosas are fine — Uncle Kareem's doctor cleared him at his follow-up, he has no dietary restrictions anymore
Lamb biryani is fine for everyone currently attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging fried samosas as problematic for Uncle Kareem — his post-surgery restriction was removed after his doctor cleared him
Flagging almond baklava as problematic for Nadia — her allergy is to peanuts, not all nuts or tree nuts generally
Flagging any dish for Omar's lactose intolerance — Omar dropped out and is no longer attending
Saying Nadia has a general nut allergy or seafood allergy — she specifically has a peanut allergy from the peanut satay incident
Flagging lamb biryani as problematic for anyone
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint reasoning across 9 turns of Eid feast planning. The agent must track: (1) Fatima is seven months pregnant → inferential chain to no raw/undercooked meat, raw eggs, unpasteurized items — never explicitly stated as a dietary rule, (2) Nadia has a peanut allergy from a specific peanut satay incident — must NOT over-generalize to all nuts (almond baklava trap), (3) Uncle Kareem's post-surgery restriction on rich/fried food is REMOVED when his doctor clears him — fried samosas become fine (constraint removal trap), (4) Omar JOINS with lactose intolerance then EXITS — his constraint disappears entirely, (5) Auntie Salma JOINS late (turn 5) with celiac disease — a late-joining high-constraint entity that models often forget. At probe time, the current constraint state is: Fatima=pregnant (no raw meat), Nadia=peanut allergy only, Auntie Salma=celiac (no wheat/barley/gluten). Uncle Kareem has NO restrictions. Omar is not attending. The 6-item probe has mixed verdicts: 2 clearly problematic (peanut sauce, raw kibbeh), 1 problematic for late-joiner (pita for Salma), 1 over-generalization trap (almond baklava looks bad but is fine), 1 removed-constraint trap (fried samosas look bad for Kareem but he is cleared), and 1 clearly fine (lamb biryani).

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
